text:
Self-evolving prompts are the biggest engineering trap in the agent space right now.

Everyone wants a system that tunes itself. 
I spent 40 hours building a self-tuning cold-outreach agent to see exactly where the logic breaks. 

The bottleneck is the evaluation gap, not the LLM's writing skill.

Most developers let the LLM grade its own work or use another LLM as a judge. 
This creates a circular hallucination engine. 
The model starts optimizing for what it thinks looks correct. 
It's a feedback loop of pure vibes. 
The system prompt tripled in size while accuracy flatlined at 62%.

You can't trust an LLM to grade its own evolution without a ground-truth feedback loop. 
True self-improvement requires an external anchor. 
Did the code actually compile, or did the LLM just say it looked 'clean'?
Hard database state changes. 
Verified golden sets that the model can't argue with.

Access to a meta-agent without a rigid metric is just a well-equipped system that can't think. 
Stop optimizing for LLM-perceived quality. 
Build the evaluation harness before you build the evolution logic.

How do you anchor your agent's evaluation when the output isn't binary?

#AIEngineering #LLMOps #AIagents
idea_source: How I built a self-improving AI agent that evolves its own prompts
